after.title: Rules: the booth and the crowd
after.text:
The loop: aim at the moving spooks, fire, and keep the streak clean. The crowd's cheer is the clock, the ammo and the ending.

Aim and fire
- The crosshair sits exactly where the pointer is; one click or tap fires one shot.
- No ammo, no reload. A shot's only cost is the crowd's patience.
- A shot is a hit anywhere on a target's painted shape. One shot destroys that target.

Hits and escapes
- A target that leaves the booth without being hit is an escape. The booth keeps targets coming and never falls silent.
- Every target type pays the same. The ghost, the pumpkin and the bat differ only in how they move and how hard they are to hit.

The crowd's cheer
- The cheer is the one meter besides the score. It starts full and drains slowly all the time; it drops hard when a shot hits nothing and when a target escapes, and every hit pays it back.
- When the cheer empties the curtain falls and the round ends. There is no clock, no lives and no round counter: the cheer is the clock, the ammo and the ending, so only a clean show keeps the night going.

The streak
- Every hit extends the streak, and the streak's length is the multiplier for that hit: a longer streak pays more per hit and pays back more cheer.
- A shot that hits nothing, or an escape, breaks the streak to nothing.

author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=systems
summary: added section “Rules: prizes and the night”

after.title: Rules: prizes and the night
after.text:
Prize targets
- Now and then a prize target enters the booth: a ghost, a pumpkin or a bat wearing a halo. It is the only target worth more than a normal one.
- Shooting a prize target pays a large chunk of the score and starts that type's powerup at once, for a short burst. Haloes appear only while no powerup is running.
- Ghost's halo, the Spectral Slug: a hit leaps to the nearest other target, then to the next, and on until the booth is empty.
- Pumpkin's halo, the Candy Buckshot: a shot covers a wide wedge around the crosshair and hits every target in it.
- Bat's halo, Moonstruck: the booth and its targets slow to a crawl while the crosshair stays quick.

The night
- The booth gets faster as it goes: more targets, faster targets, quicker escapes, and a crowd that tires sooner.
- The results show the takings, the longest streak, the prizes taken and a prize stamp. The best score is saved, and the next stamp is the reason to step back up.

author: claude
summary: edited section “Rules: the booth and the crowd”

before.title: Rules: the booth and the crowd
before.text:
The loop: aim at the moving spooks, fire, and keep the streak clean. The crowd's cheer is the clock, the ammo and the ending.

Aim and fire
- The crosshair is the pointer: under the cursor on a mouse, an offset above the finger on touch, so the target is never hidden. The shot lands where the crosshair is.
- One click or tap fires one shot. No ammo and no reload: a shot's only cost is the crowd's patience.
- A shot is a hit anywhere on a target's painted shape. One shot destroys that target.

Hits and escapes
- A target that leaves the booth without being hit is an escape. The booth keeps the targets coming and never falls silent.
- Every target type pays the same. The ghost, the pumpkin and the bat differ only in how they move and how hard they are to hit.
- The first few escapes of a night cost no cheer, and the first cue tells the player that this one is free and what the next one will cost.

The crowd's cheer
- The cheer is the one meter besides the score. It starts full and drains all the time; the drain climbs with the night's acts, so every show ends eventually, however clean.
- It drops hard when a shot hits nothing and when an escape happens, and every hit pays it back. The payback grows with the streak but is capped well below the score multiplier, so a perfect streak slows the drain without cancelling it.
- When the cheer empties the curtain falls and the round ends. There is no countdown, no lives and no round counter: the cheer is the clock, the ammo and the ending.

The streak
- Every hit extends the streak, and the streak's length is the score multiplier for that hit.
- A shot that hits nothing, or an escape, breaks the streak to nothing.

author: claude
summary: edited section “Rules: prizes and the night”

before.title: Rules: prizes and the night
before.text:
Prize targets
- Now and then a prize target enters the booth: a ghost, a pumpkin or a bat wearing a halo. It is the only target worth more than a normal one.
- Shooting a prize target pays a large chunk of the score and starts that type's powerup at once, for a short burst. Haloes appear only while no powerup is running.
- Ghost's halo, the Spectral Slug: a hit leaps to the nearest other target, then to the next, and keeps leaping while the next target is within the ghost's reach; a scattered booth stops the leap.
- Pumpkin's halo, the Candy Buckshot: a shot covers a wide wedge around the crosshair and hits every target in it.
- Bat's halo, Moonstruck: the booth and its targets slow to a crawl and the crowd holds its breath — the cheer stops draining for the burst. The hardest target to hit carries the prize that can save a show on its last legs.

The night's acts
- The night plays in three acts on a fixed pace; each act opens with a marquee cue and steps up: the booth runs faster and the crowd's drain climbs.
- The last act is the booth at full speed and the crowd at its pickiest. Every show ends: the last act's drain is more than the best play can pay back, so a clean night still closes.

The results
- The curtain shows the takings, the longest streak, the prizes taken and the stamps earned. The best score is saved.
- Stamps, each one named on the results: Hot Streak — a streak that reaches the top of the multiplier. Prize Parade — all three prizes in one night. Ghost Train — a Slug leap that clears every target in the booth. Last Act — reaching the third act.

before.title: Rules: prizes and the night
before.text:
Prize targets
- Now and then a prize target enters the booth: a ghost, a pumpkin or a bat wearing a halo. It is the only target worth more than a normal one.
- Shooting a prize target pays a large chunk of the score and starts that type's powerup at once, for a burst long enough to enjoy.
- Haloes arrive on a steady cadence, dealt from a shuffled bag of the three types, so no prize repeats until the other two have had their turn. A halo only appears while no powerup is running; if one is running it waits.
- Ghost's halo, the Spectral Slug: a hit leaps to the nearest other target, then to the next, and keeps leaping while the next target is within the ghost's reach; a scattered booth stops the leap.
- Pumpkin's halo, the Candy Buckshot: a shot covers a wide wedge around the crosshair and hits every target in it.
- Bat's halo, Moonstruck: the booth and its targets slow to a crawl and the crowd holds its breath — the passive drain stops for the burst, while hits still score and still pay cheer and misses and escapes still cost. Only the drain pauses, never the act clock. The hardest target to hit carries the prize that can rescue a show on its last legs.

The night's acts
- The night plays in three acts on the show's own clock, which never pauses, not even for a powerup. Each act opens with a marquee cue and steps up: the booth spawns more and faster targets and the crowd's drain climbs.
- The booth spawns on its own schedule and never waits for the player to clear it, and it keeps a floor of live targets. An escape therefore always means the player let one through, never that the booth starved them at the wrong rate.
- The last act is the booth at full speed and the crowd at its pickiest. Every show ends: the last act's drain is more than the best play can pay back, so a clean night still closes.

The results
- The curtain shows the takings, the longest streak, the prizes taken and the stamps earned. The best score is saved.
- Stamps, each one named on the results: Hot Streak — a streak that reaches the top of the multiplier. Prize Parade — all three prizes in one night. Ghost Train — a Slug chain of several targets in one leap. Last Act — reaching the third act.

after.title: Tuning starting values (from Systems, latest)
after.text:
First-pass constants for the prototype; all editable, all untested. Previously only in chat.
- Cheer: starts 100. Passive drain per second: act 1 = 1, act 2 = 2, act 3 = 3.5. Acts begin at 0 / 50 / 100 s.
- Payback per hit: +1.0 plus 0.1 per streak step, capped at 1.5 (reached at streak 5). Wild shot: -2 cheer and streak halved. Escape: -4 cheer, streak untouched; first two escapes of a night are free.
- Score multiplier: equals the streak, capped at 10x.
- Spawns per second: 1.3 / 1.5 / 1.8, with a floor of 3 live targets.
- Halo about every 15 s from a shuffled bag; powerup burst about 4 s (Open Questions suggest trying about 8 s).
- Expected: average player dies near 90 s, a strong one near 145 s.
Still undefined and needed before building: prize score value, Candy Buckshot wedge angle and radius, Slug leap reach, Moonstruck slow factor, target speeds per type, hit-shape forgiveness in act one.

author: claude
summary: edited section “Rules: prizes and the night”

before.title: Rules: prizes and the night
before.text:
Prize targets
- Now and then a prize target enters the booth: a ghost, a pumpkin or a bat wearing a halo. It is the only target worth more than a normal one.
- Shooting a prize target pays a large chunk of the score and starts that type's powerup at once, for a burst long enough to enjoy.
- Haloes arrive on a steady cadence, dealt from a shuffled bag of the three types, so no prize repeats until the other two have had their turn. A halo only appears while no powerup is running; if one is running it waits.
- Ghost's halo, the Spectral Slug: a hit leaps to the nearest other target, then to the next, and keeps leaping while the next target is within the ghost's reach; a scattered booth stops the leap.
- Pumpkin's halo, the Candy Buckshot: a shot covers a wide wedge around the crosshair and hits every target in it.
- Bat's halo, Moonstruck: the booth and its targets slow to a crawl and the crowd holds its breath — the passive drain stops for the burst, while hits still score and still pay cheer and misses and escapes still cost. Only the drain pauses, never the act clock. The hardest target to hit carries the prize that can rescue a show on its last legs.
- Each target a powerup fells counts as its own hit: it extends the streak and pays its own score and cheer, and the streak runs on through the burst.

The night's acts
- The night plays in three acts on the show's own clock, which never pauses, not even for a powerup. Each act opens with a marquee cue and steps up: the booth spawns more and faster targets and the crowd's drain climbs.
- The booth spawns on its own schedule and never waits for the player to clear it, and it keeps a floor of live targets. An escape therefore always means the player let one through, never that the booth starved them at the wrong rate.
- The last act is the booth at full speed and the crowd at its pickiest. Every show ends: the last act's drain is more than the best play can pay back, so a clean night still closes.

The results
- The curtain shows the takings, the longest streak, the prizes taken and the stamps earned. The best score is saved.
- Stamps, each one named on the results: Hot Streak — a streak that reaches the top of the multiplier. Prize Parade — all three prizes in one night. Ghost Train — a Slug chain of several targets in one leap. Last Act — reaching the third act.

before.title: Tuning starting values (from Systems, latest)
before.text:
First-pass constants for the prototype; all editable, all untested. Previously only in chat.
- Cheer: starts 100. Passive drain per second: act 1 = 1, act 2 = 2, act 3 = 3.5. Acts begin at 0 / 50 / 100 s.
- Payback per hit: +1.0 plus 0.1 per streak step, capped at 1.5 (reached at streak 5). Wild shot: -2 cheer and streak halved. Escape: -4 cheer, streak untouched; first two escapes of a night are free.
- Score multiplier: equals the streak, capped at 10x.
- Spawns per second: 1.3 / 1.5 / 1.8, with a floor of 3 live targets.
- Halo about every 15 s from a shuffled bag; powerup burst about 4 s (Open Questions suggest trying about 8 s).
- Expected: average player dies near 90 s, a strong one near 145 s.
Still undefined and needed before building: prize score value, Candy Buckshot wedge angle and radius, Slug leap reach, Moonstruck slow factor, target speeds per type, hit-shape forgiveness in act one.

summary: edited section “Open Questions”

before.title: Open Questions
before.text:
- Stopwatch test with two real players: does an average player last about 90–120 seconds, and a strong one reach act three? Log escapes per minute, average streak length (target about 5), shots per second and accuracy, and the share of bats an experienced player shoots (under half means bats need a bigger escape cost or a graze rule).
- Does spraying (above about 3 shots a second) survive act one? If so, a wild shot costs too little at low streaks.
- Do first-time touch players reach a streak of 5 at least once? If not, make the hit shape more forgiving in act one.
- Can a thumb reach the touch-cancel area on a full-screen phone without covering the crosshair?
- Are powerup bursts long enough to enjoy (try about 8 seconds, or a shot count for the Buckshot)?
- Does one Slug chain or Buckshot blast restore most of the cheer meter? If so, powerup kills pay less cheer.
- Can a new player say why they lost after the first night?
- What chain length earns Ghost Train in a normal booth?

author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=systems
summary: edited section “Rules: the booth and the crowd”

before.title: Rules: the booth and the crowd
before.text:
The loop: aim at the moving spooks, fire, and keep the streak clean. The crowd's cheer is the clock, the ammo and the ending.

Aim and fire
- Mouse: the crosshair is under the cursor; a click fires there.
- Touch: a quick tap fires at the tap point; dragging shows an offset crosshair above the finger and lifting the finger fires there, so the target is never hidden. Dragging off the booth cancels the shot.
- One shot per click or release. No ammo and no reload: a shot's only cost is the crowd's patience.
- A shot is a hit anywhere on a target's painted shape. One shot destroys that target.

Hits and escapes
- A target that leaves the booth without being hit is an escape. It costs cheer but never touches the streak: you can't shoot everything, so only your own wild shots cost you.
- An escape costs more cheer than a wild shot, so a shot with a real chance of landing is always better than letting the target go. What a wild shot really costs you is part of your streak.
- Every target type pays the same. The ghost, the pumpkin and the bat differ only in how they move and how hard they are to hit.
- The first two escapes of a night are free. The first cue says this one is free and that later escapes cost cheer.

The crowd's cheer
- The cheer is the one meter besides the score. It starts full and drains all the time; the drain climbs with the night's acts, so every show ends eventually, however clean.
- It drops when a shot hits nothing and when an escape happens, and every hit pays it back.
- The payback rises only over the first few hits of a streak, then holds flat while the multiplier keeps climbing. So a long streak eases the drain without ever cancelling it.
- When the cheer empties the curtain falls and the round ends. There is no countdown, no lives and no round counter.

The streak
- Every hit extends the streak, and the multiplier for a hit is the streak counting that hit, so the first hit of a night scores once and the multiplier climbs with every clean hit.
- A shot that hits nothing halves the streak, rounded down, and a wild shot at a streak of one clears it. Escapes leave the streak standing.
- No single miss wipes the multiplier, so a hard shot is always a bet the player can afford to make; the streak is worth steadying your aim for, not worth freezing over.

after.text:
First-pass constants for the prototype; all editable. The bot showed a fast, accurate shooter outruns a flat 3.5 drain, so the act-three ramp, not a starved booth, is what ends every show.

- Escape: -4 cheer, streak untouched; the first two escapes of a night are free.
- Score: a normal target pays 100 x multiplier; a prize target pays 500 x multiplier plus its powerup. Multiplier equals the streak, capped at 10x.
- Hit shape: the painted shape plus a forgiveness margin of 25% of the target's widest dimension in act 1, 12% in act 2, 5% in act 3.
- Target speed in booth widths per second: ghost 0.12 drifting, pumpkin 0.18 bouncing, bat 0.30 swooping. Act speed multiplier 1.0 / 1.2 / 1.45.
- Spawns per second: 1.3 / 1.5 / 1.8, with a floor of 3 / 4 / 5 live targets.
- Halo about every 15 s from a shuffled bag of the three types; a halo waits while a powerup runs. Every burst lasts 8 s.
- Spectral Slug reach: 20% of the booth's width, measured from the last felled target, checked against the nearest remaining target each leap.
- Candy Buckshot: fan from the muzzle at the bottom centre, centred on the crosshair, half-angle 20 degrees, reaching the top of the booth; it hits every target whose centre is inside. Applies to every shot during the burst.
- Moonstruck: everything in the booth at 25% speed, spawns and exits included; passive drain frozen; act clock keeps running.
- Average streak length in the log: the streak's value each time a wild shot halves or breaks it.

before.title: Open Questions
before.text:
- Stopwatch test with two real players, one new to touch: does an average player last about 90–120 seconds, and a strong one reach act three but not run past about 3 minutes? - Does the act-3 ramp end strong players' shows at a satisfying moment, not abruptly?
- Does one Slug chain or Buckshot blast restore most of the cheer meter? If so, powerup kills pay less cheer.
- Does Moonstruck feel like a rescue, or does the slow booth just drag?
- Can a new player say why they lost after the first night?
- What chain length earns Ghost Train in a normal booth?

after.title: Playtest 1 results (7 mouse runs)
after.text:
- Every night is far too short: 15 to 60 seconds against a 90 to 120 second target. Nobody reached act three; two runs reached act two.
- Wild shots are the biggest cheer loss in every run, bigger than the drain and the escapes. Even the 68%-accuracy run lost more to misses than to the drain. The wild-shot ladder is too harsh, as QA predicted.
- Hits pay back far too little: a hit refills less than one wild shot costs, so missing a little outweighs hitting a lot.
- Escapes are too frequent for most players (about 15 to 35 a minute), so the booth spawns faster than people can shoot.
- The streak mostly stays low: it averages 1 to 4 at each break, under the target of 5. Good runs still hit long streaks (12 and 31).
- Spraying dies fast (2.6 shots a second at 18% accuracy died in 15 seconds), so the anti-spray rule works and can be softened.
- Weaker players skip bats (10 to 27% shot); stronger ones shoot about half.
- Ghost Train is reachable: one Slug chain hit 7.
- Touch is untested: every shot was a mouse click.
- The build's tuning differs from the Brief in places (act-one hit margin, prize score, Buckshot width, Moonstruck speed); match it to the Brief before the next test.

summary: edited section “Rules: the booth and the crowd”

before.title: Rules: the booth and the crowd
before.text:
The loop: aim at the moving spooks, fire, and keep the streak clean. The crowd's cheer is the clock, the ammo and the ending.

Aim and fire
- Mouse: the crosshair is under the cursor; a click fires there.
- Touch: a quick tap fires at the tap point; dragging shows an offset crosshair above the finger and lifting the finger fires there, so the target is never hidden. Dragging off the booth cancels the shot.
- One shot per click or release. No ammo and no reload: a shot's only cost is the crowd's patience.
- A shot is a hit anywhere on a target's painted shape, plus a forgiveness margin around it that is generous in act one and tighter in each later act. One shot destroys that target.

Hits and escapes
- A target that leaves the booth without being hit is an escape. It costs cheer but never touches the streak: you can't shoot everything, so only your own wild shots cost you.
- A single wild shot costs less cheer than an escape, so a shot with a real chance of landing is still better than letting the target go. Wild shots in a row get dearer each time: the crowd spots a flail.
- Every target type pays the same. The ghost, the pumpkin and the bat differ only in how they move and how hard they are to hit.
- The first two escapes of a night are free. The first cue says this one is free and that later escapes cost cheer.

The crowd's cheer

before.title: Rules: prizes and the night
before.text:

- Now and then a prize target enters the booth: a ghost, a pumpkin or a bat wearing a halo. It is the only target worth more than a normal one.

before.title: Tuning starting values (from Systems, latest)
before.text:
First-pass constants for the prototype; all editable. The bot showed a fast, accurate shooter outruns a flat 3.5 drain, so the act-three ramp, not a starved booth, is what ends every show.
- Cheer: starts 100. Passive drain per second: act 1 = 1, act 2 = 2, act 3 starts at 3.5 and rises 0.03 every second with no ceiling. Acts begin at 0 / 50 / 100 s.
- Payback per hit: +1.0 plus 0.1 per streak step, capped at 1.5 (reached at streak 5).
- Wild shot: cheer cost 2, then 4, then 8, and 8 for each further miss in a row, resetting to 2 on any hit; the streak halves.
- Escape: -4 cheer, streak untouched; the first two escapes of a night are free.
- Score: a normal target pays 100 x multiplier; a prize target pays 500 x multiplier plus its powerup. Multiplier equals the streak, capped at 10x.
- Hit shape: the painted shape plus a forgiveness margin of 25% of the target's widest dimension in act 1, 12% in act 2, 5% in act 3.
- Target speed in booth widths per second: ghost 0.12 drifting, pumpkin 0.18 bouncing, bat 0.30 swooping. Act speed multiplier 1.0 / 1.2 / 1.45.
- Spawns per second: 1.3 / 1.5 / 1.8, with a floor of 3 / 4 / 5 live targets.
- Halo about every 15 s from a shuffled bag of the three types; a halo waits while a powerup runs. Every burst lasts 8 s.
- Spectral Slug reach: 20% of the booth's width, measured from the last felled target, checked against the nearest remaining target each leap.
- Candy Buckshot: fan from the muzzle at the bottom centre, centred on the crosshair, half-angle 20 degrees, reaching the top of the booth; it hits every target whose centre is inside. Applies to every shot during the burst.
- Moonstruck: everything in the booth at 25% speed, spawns and exits included; passive drain frozen; act clock keeps running.
- Average streak length in the log: the streak's value each time a wild shot halves or breaks it.
- Expected: average player dies near 90 s, a strong one near 145 s. Bot check: at 3 shots a second with 50% accuracy, the wild-shot ladder should end the night inside act one.

before.title: Playtest 1 results (7 mouse runs)
before.text:
- Every night is far too short: 15 to 60 seconds against a 90 to 120 second target. Nobody reached act three; two runs reached act two.
- Wild shots are the biggest cheer loss in every run, bigger than the drain and the escapes. Even the 68%-accuracy run lost more to misses than to the drain. The wild-shot ladder is too harsh, as QA predicted.
- Hits pay back far too little: a hit refills less than one wild shot costs, so missing a little outweighs hitting a lot.
- Escapes are too frequent for most players (about 15 to 35 a minute), so the booth spawns faster than people can shoot.
- The streak mostly stays low: it averages 1 to 4 at each break, under the target of 5. Good runs still hit long streaks (12 and 31).
- Spraying dies fast (2.6 shots a second at 18% accuracy died in 15 seconds), so the anti-spray rule works and can be softened.
- Weaker players skip bats (10 to 27% shot); stronger ones shoot about half.
- Ghost Train is reachable: one Slug chain hit 7.
- Touch is untested: every shot was a mouse click.
- The build's tuning differs from the Brief in places (act-one hit margin, prize score, Buckshot width, Moonstruck speed); match it to the Brief before the next test.

before.text:

author: claude
summary: edited section “Rules: prizes and the night”

before.title: Rules: prizes and the night
before.text:
Prize targets
- Now and then a prize target enters the booth: a ghost, a pumpkin or a bat wearing a halo. It is the only target worth more than a normal one.
- Shooting a prize target pays a large chunk of the score and starts that type's powerup at once, for a burst of a few seconds.
- Haloes arrive on a steady cadence, dealt from a shuffled bag of the three types, so no prize repeats until the other two have had their turn. A halo only appears while no powerup is running; if one is running it waits.
- Ghost's halo, the Spectral Slug: for the whole burst, every shot that lands becomes a chain — it fells its target and leaps to the nearest other target, and on to the next while each is within the ghost's reach; a scattered booth stops the leap.
- Pumpkin's halo, the Candy Buckshot: for the whole burst, every shot is a fan that starts at the gun at the bottom centre of the booth, opens through the crosshair in a wide wedge, and fells every target inside that wedge.
- Bat's halo, Moonstruck: the whole booth slows to half speed — targets move, arrive and leave at the same slow pace, so the booth neither floods nor empties — and the crowd holds its breath, with the passive drain running at half rate. Only the drain is eased, never the act clock. The hardest target to hit carries the prize that can rescue a show on its last legs.
- Each target a powerup fells counts as its own hit: it extends the streak and pays its own cheer. Extra targets felled by a chain or a fan pay a flat score each rather than the multiplier, so the multiplier stays the reward for aimed shots and a burst cannot outscore the shooting around it.
- A shot fired during a burst that fells nothing is a wild shot like any other, at the same cheer cost and the same halving of the streak.

The night's acts
- The night plays in three acts on the show's own clock, which never pauses, not even for a powerup. Each act opens with a marquee cue and steps up: the booth spawns more and faster targets and the crowd's drain climbs.
- The booth spawns on its own schedule and never waits for the player to clear it, and it keeps a floor of live targets. An escape therefore always means the player let one through, never that the booth starved them at the wrong rate.
- The ending does not rely on the booth running dry. In the last act the drain keeps rising the longer the show runs, with no ceiling, so sooner or later it outruns the best payback and the curtain falls.

The results
- The curtain shows the takings, the longest streak, the prizes taken and the stamps earned. The best score is saved.
- Stamps, each one named on the results: Hot Streak — a streak that reaches the top of the multiplier. Prize Parade — all three prizes in one night. Ghost Train — a Slug chain of several targets in one leap. Last Act — reaching the third act. These four names are the only stamps; every screen uses them.

author: claude
summary: edited section “Open Questions”

before.title: Open Questions
before.text:
- Re-tune check: does the median player (under half their shots landing) reach act two with cheer to spare and last 90–120 seconds? Does a strong one reach act three but stop before about 3 minutes?
- Touch test with a first-time touch player: offset crosshair, tap to fire, drag to cancel, reaching a streak of 5. This is the biggest untested risk.
- After the re-tune, do weaker players still skip bats (under half shot)?
- Does the act-3 ramp end strong players' shows at a satisfying moment, not abruptly?
- Does one Slug chain or Buckshot blast restore most of the cheer meter?
- Does Moonstruck feel like a rescue, or does the slow booth just drag?
- Can a new player say why they lost after the first night?
- Does the game need a pause / quit option during a night? The flowchart has none.

after.title: Open Questions
after.text:
- DISPUTED (QA, 18:02): on the third-pass numbers the median player (44%, 1.75 shots/s) loses about 2.7 cheer a second in act two (escapes are the line the tuning estimate left out) and dies near 85 s, not the 110–120 s in the tuning section. QA's proposed fix: escapes cost 2 in acts one and two, 4 in act three; act-two drain 1. Systems has not answered.
- Re-tune check: does the median player (under half their shots landing) reach act two with cheer to spare and last 90–120 seconds? Does a strong one reach act three but stop before about 3 minutes?
- Touch test with a first-time touch player: offset crosshair, tap to fire, drag to cancel, reaching a streak of 5. This is the biggest untested risk. What separates a tap from a drag is not yet defined.
- After the re-tune, do weaker players still skip bats (under half shot)?
- Does the act-3 ramp end strong players' shows at a satisfying moment, not abruptly?
- Does one Slug chain or Buckshot blast restore most of the cheer meter?
- Does Moonstruck feel like a rescue, or does the slow booth just drag? On paper it halves spawns and so roughly halves hit payback along with the drain; it may be worth almost nothing.
- What happens when a prize target escapes: does it cost cheer like any escape, and does its type go back in the bag or is it lost until the bag refills?
- With act one's flat 1-cheer miss and 2.5+ payback, firing is cheer-positive above about 27% accuracy. Does fast sweeping in act one become the survival strategy?
- Can a new player say why they lost after the first night?
- Does the game need a pause / quit option during a night? The flowchart has none. At minimum, a browser tab losing focus must not let the never-pausing clock and drain kill the player.

before.title: Tuning starting values (from Systems, third pass)
before.text:
Third pass, tuned for the median logged player: 44% accuracy at about 1.75 shots a second (seven mouse runs: 18–68% accuracy, nights of 15–60 s, wild shots eating 52–92 cheer). All editable. What changed and why: the wild shot is now a quarter of an escape instead of half, so a hit pays back far more than a miss costs; act-one drain stays put but the miss ladder is flat there; act two's drain drops and its ladder stops at 4, so the ladder that killed playtest 1 only reaches full strength in act three.

- Cheer: 100, never above 100. Passive drain per second: act 1 = 1, act 2 = 1.5, act 3 starts at 3 and rises 0.06 every second with no ceiling. Acts begin at 0 / 50 / 100 s.
- Payback per hit: 2.5 plus 0.25 per streak step, capped at 3.5 (reached at streak 4). One hit is worth two and a half wild shots.
- Wild shot cost: 1 cheer, flat, for all of act one. Act two: 1, then 2, then 4, capped at 4. Act three: 1, 2, 4, then 8, capped at 8. Any hit resets it to the first step. The streak halves. A burst shot that fells nothing counts as a wild shot.
- Escape: 4 cheer, streak untouched; the first two escapes of a night are free.
- Streak and multiplier: the streak stops at 10, which is also the top multiplier; a hit's multiplier is the streak counting that hit, so 10x is the highest a hit can score.
- Score: a normal target pays 100 x multiplier; a prize target pays 500 x multiplier plus its powerup; every extra target felled by a chain or fan pays a flat 150.
- Hit shape: the painted shape plus a margin of 25% of the target's widest dimension in act 1, 12% in act 2, 5% in act 3.
- Target speed in booth widths per second: ghost 0.12 drifting, pumpkin 0.18 bouncing, bat 0.30 swooping. Act speed multiplier 1.0 / 1.2 / 1.45.
- Spawns per second: 0.9 / 1.1 / 1.4, with a floor of 2 / 3 / 3 live targets. Act one spawns below the median player's hit rate, so escapes should fall from 15–35 a minute to under 10.
- Halo about every 25 s from a shuffled bag of the three types, so bursts cover under a quarter of the night; a halo waits while a burst runs. Every burst lasts 6 s.
- Spectral Slug reach: 20% of the booth's width, measured from the last felled target and re-checked against the nearest remaining target on each leap.
- Candy Buckshot: fan from the muzzle at the bottom centre, centred on the crosshair, half-angle 20 degrees, reaching the top of the booth; it fells every target whose centre is inside. Applies to every shot during the burst.
- Moonstruck: everything in the booth at half speed, spawns and exits included, and the passive drain at half rate; the act clock keeps running.
- Average streak length in the log: the streak's value each time a wild shot halves or breaks it.

Expectations for this pass (paper estimates, to be checked against the next log): the median 44% player ends act one near 90 cheer and dies around 110–120 s, in early act three; a 30% player still dies inside act one near 45 s; a 68% player dies around 170–175 s, just inside the 3-minute cap; spam-clicking still dies inside act one.

summary: edited section “Rules: the booth and the crowd”

before.title: Rules: the booth and the crowd
before.text:
The loop: aim at the moving spooks, fire, and keep the streak clean. The crowd's cheer is the clock, the ammo and the ending.

Aim and fire
- Mouse: the crosshair is under the cursor; a click fires there.
- Touch: a quick tap fires at the tap point; dragging shows an offset crosshair above the finger and lifting the finger fires there, so the target is never hidden. Dragging off the booth cancels the shot.
- One shot per click or release. No ammo and no reload: a shot's only cost is the crowd's patience.
- A shot is a hit anywhere on a target's painted shape, plus a forgiveness margin around it that is generous in act one and tighter in each later act. One shot destroys that target.

Hits and escapes
- A target that leaves the booth without being hit is an escape. It costs cheer but never touches the streak: you can't shoot everything, so only your own wild shots cost you.
- A hit pays back more cheer than a single wild shot costs, so accurate shooting is always the way to keep the crowd. A single wild shot is also cheaper than an escape, so a shot with a real chance of landing beats letting the target go. Only a run of misses in a row can cost more than a hit repays: the crowd spots a flail.
- Every target type pays the same. The ghost, the pumpkin and the bat differ only in how they move and how hard they are to hit.
- The first two escapes of a night are free. The first cue says this one is free and that later escapes cost cheer.

The crowd's cheer
- The cheer is the one meter besides the score. It starts full and can never rise above full; it drains all the time, and the drain climbs with the night's acts, so every show ends eventually, however clean.
- Misses in a row get dearer only as the night goes on: flat in act one, a small step up in act two, and the full ladder only in act three. Any hit resets the cost to its first step.
- It drops on a shot that hits nothing and on an escape, and every hit pays it back.
- The payback rises only over the first few hits of a streak, then holds flat while the multiplier keeps climbing. So a long streak eases the drain without ever cancelling it.
- When the cheer empties the curtain falls and the round ends. There is no countdown, no lives and no round counter.

The streak
- Every hit extends the streak, and the multiplier for a hit is the streak counting that hit, so the first hit of a night scores once and the multiplier climbs with every clean hit.
- The streak stops climbing at the top of the multiplier, so the longest streak and the best multiplier are the same height and a miss anywhere on the ladder really costs.
- A shot that hits nothing halves the streak, rounded down, and a wild shot at a streak of one clears it. Escapes leave the streak standing.
- No single miss wipes the multiplier, so a hard shot is always a bet the player can afford to make; the streak is worth steadying your aim for, not worth freezing over.

author: claude
summary: edited section “Open Questions”

before.title: Open Questions
before.text:
- DISPUTED (QA, 18:02): on the third-pass numbers the median player (44%, 1.75 shots/s) loses about 2.7 cheer a second in act two (escapes are the line the tuning estimate left out) and dies near 85 s, not the 110–120 s in the tuning section. QA's proposed fix: escapes cost 2 in acts one and two, 4 in act three; act-two drain 1. Systems has not answered.
- Re-tune check: does the median player (under half their shots landing) reach act two with cheer to spare and last 90–120 seconds? Does a strong one reach act three but stop before about 3 minutes?
- Touch test with a first-time touch player: offset crosshair, tap to fire, drag to cancel, reaching a streak of 5. This is the biggest untested risk. What separates a tap from a drag is not yet defined.
- After the re-tune, do weaker players still skip bats (under half shot)?
- Does the act-3 ramp end strong players' shows at a satisfying moment, not abruptly?
- Does one Slug chain or Buckshot blast restore most of the cheer meter?
- Does Moonstruck feel like a rescue, or does the slow booth just drag? On paper it halves spawns and so roughly halves hit payback along with the drain; it may be worth almost nothing.
- What happens when a prize target escapes: does it cost cheer like any escape, and does its type go back in the bag or is it lost until the bag refills?
- With act one's flat 1-cheer miss and 2.5+ payback, firing is cheer-positive above about 27% accuracy. Does fast sweeping in act one become the survival strategy?
- Can a new player say why they lost after the first night?
- Does the game need a pause / quit option during a night? The flowchart has none. At minimum, a browser tab losing focus must not let the never-pausing clock and drain kill the player.

after.title: Open Questions
after.text:
- Re-tune check: does the median player (under half their shots landing) reach act two with cheer to spare and last 90–120 seconds? Does a strong one reach act three but stop before about 3 minutes?
- Touch test with a first-time touch player: offset crosshair, tap to fire, drag to cancel, reaching a streak of 5. This is the biggest untested risk. Still undefined: what separates a tap from a drag; how the raised crosshair reaches the top edge of the booth; and, since the crosshair sits above the finger, aiming at the bottom edge puts the finger off the booth, which the rules say cancels the shot.
- After the re-tune, do weaker players still skip bats (under half shot)? If so, Moonstruck, the rescue powerup, rarely reaches the players who need rescuing.
- Does the act-3 ramp end strong players' shows at a satisfying moment, not abruptly? On paper the median player's act three lasts only about 6 seconds.
- Does one Slug chain or Buckshot blast restore most of the cheer meter?
- Is Moonstruck worth chasing before act three? In acts one and two the drain it stops is 1 a second, so a burst saves about 6 cheer, or nothing when cheer is already near full. Late in act three it saves about 40.
- Hits can't outpace spawns (0.9 a second in act one), so firing faster mostly adds misses. Confirm in the log that fast sweepers don't outlast aimers in act one.
- Can a new player say why they lost after the first night?
- Does the game need a pause / quit option during a night? The flowchart has none. At minimum, a browser tab losing focus must not let the never-pausing clock and drain kill the player.

before.title: Tuning starting values (from Systems, fourth pass)
before.text:
Fourth pass. QA's act-two check was right: the third pass left escapes out of the act-two sum and lost about 1.3 cheer a second to them. Adopted as QA proposed: an escape costs 2 in acts one and two and 4 only in act three, and act two's drain is 1. Also adopted: the forgiveness margin no longer shrinks, so act two's felt accuracy stays at the logged 44%. All values editable.

- Cheer: 100, never above 100. Passive drain per second: act 1 = 1, act 2 = 1, act 3 starts at 3.5 and rises 0.07 every second with no ceiling. Acts begin at 0 / 50 / 100 s.
- Payback per hit: 2.5 for the first hit of a streak, plus 0.25 for each further step, capped at 3.5 (reached at streak 5).
- Wild shot cost: 1 cheer, flat, for all of act one. Act two: 1, then 2, then 4, capped at 4. Act three: 1, 2, 4, then 8, capped at 8. Any hit resets it to the first step. The streak halves. A burst shot that fells nothing counts as a wild shot.
- Escape: 2 cheer in acts one and two, 4 in act three; the streak is untouched and the first two escapes of a night are free.
- Streak and multiplier: the streak stops at 10, which is also the top multiplier; a hit's multiplier is the streak counting that hit, so 10x is the highest a hit can score.
- Score: a normal target pays 100 x multiplier; a prize target pays 500 x multiplier plus its powerup; every extra target felled by a chain or fan pays a flat 150.
- Hit shape: the painted shape plus a margin of 25% of the target's widest dimension, the same in every act. Later acts are harder only through speed, spawn rate and drain.
- Target speed in booth widths per second: ghost 0.12 drifting, pumpkin 0.18 bouncing, bat 0.30 swooping. Act speed multiplier 1.0 / 1.2 / 1.45.
- Spawns per second: 0.9 / 1.0 / 1.3, with a floor of 2 / 3 / 3 live targets. Act one spawns below the median player's hit rate, so escapes should fall from 15–35 a minute to under 10.
- Halo about every 25 s from a shuffled bag of the three types, so bursts cover under a quarter of the night; a halo waits while a burst runs. Every burst lasts 6 s.
- Spectral Slug reach: 20% of the booth's width, measured from the last felled target and re-checked against the nearest remaining target on each leap.
- Candy Buckshot: fan from the muzzle at the bottom centre, centred on the crosshair, half-angle 20 degrees, reaching the top of the booth; it fells every target whose centre is inside. Applies to every shot during the burst.
- Moonstruck: for the 6 s burst, targets move at half speed and the passive drain is zero; the booth keeps spawning on its normal schedule and the act clock keeps running. Misses and escapes cost the same as ever. Because a target at half speed stays on screen twice as long, the booth fills up while the bleed stops — the rescue powerup.
- Ghost Train needs a Slug chain of 5 or more targets from one shot.
- Average streak length in the log: the streak's value each time a wild shot halves or breaks it.

Expected night for the median logged player (44% accuracy, about 1.75 shots a second, cheer per second):
- Act one: payback +2.3, misses −1.0, escapes −0.3, drain −1.0, net about +0.1 — they enter act two near full.
- Act two: payback +2.3, misses −2.2 (the 1-2-4 ladder), escapes −0.5, drain −1.0, net about −1.4 — they enter act three near 30 cheer.
- Act three: payback +2.3, misses −2.2, escapes −0.9, drain −3.5 and rising, net about −4.3 — the show ends within a few seconds.
- Night length: about 105–110 s. A 33% player dies around 65–70 s in act two; a 85% player dies around 165 s, inside the 3-minute cap; spam-clicking (3 shots a second at 18%) still dies in act one near 40 s.

before.title: Tuning starting values (from Systems, fourth pass)
before.text:
Fourth pass. QA's act-two check was right: the third pass left escapes out of the act-two sum and lost about 1.3 cheer a second to them. Adopted as QA proposed: an escape costs 2 in acts one and two and 4 only in act three, and act two's drain is 1. Also adopted: the forgiveness margin no longer shrinks, so act two's felt accuracy stays at the logged 44%. All values editable.

- Cheer: 100, never above 100. Passive drain per second: act 1 = 1, act 2 = 1, act 3 starts at 3.5 and rises 0.07 every second with no ceiling. Acts begin at 0 / 50 / 100 s.
- Payback per hit: 2.5 for the first hit of a streak, plus 0.25 for each further step, capped at 3.5 (reached at streak 5).
- Wild shot cost: 1 cheer, flat, for all of act one. Act two: 1, then 2, then 4, capped at 4. Act three: 1, 2, 4, then 8, capped at 8. Any hit resets it to the first step. The streak halves. A burst shot that fells nothing counts as a wild shot.
- Escape: 2 cheer in acts one and two, 4 in act three; the streak is untouched and the first two escapes of a night are free.
- Streak and multiplier: the streak stops at 10, which is also the top multiplier; a hit's multiplier is the streak counting that hit, so 10x is the highest a hit can score.
- Score: a normal target pays 100 x multiplier; a prize target pays 500 x multiplier plus its powerup; every extra target felled by a chain or fan pays a flat 150.
- Hit shape: the painted shape plus a margin of 25% of the target's widest dimension, the same in every act. Later acts are harder only through speed, spawn rate and drain.
- Target speed in booth widths per second: ghost 0.12 drifting, pumpkin 0.18 bouncing, bat 0.30 swooping. Act speed multiplier 1.0 / 1.2 / 1.45.
- Spawns per second: 0.9 / 1.0 / 1.3, with a floor of 2 / 3 / 3 live targets. Act one spawns just above the median player's hit rate (about 0.77 hits a second), so escapes should fall from 15–35 a minute to under 10. Hits can never outpace spawns, so the strongest players are capped by the spawn rate, not their aim.
- Halo about every 25 s from a shuffled bag of the three types, so bursts cover under a quarter of the night; a halo waits while a burst runs. Every burst lasts 6 s.
- Spectral Slug reach: 20% of the booth's width, measured from the last felled target and re-checked against the nearest remaining target on each leap.
- Candy Buckshot: fan from the muzzle at the bottom centre, centred on the crosshair, half-angle 20 degrees, reaching the top of the booth; it fells every target whose centre is inside. Applies to every shot during the burst.
- Moonstruck: for the 6 s burst, targets move at half speed and the passive drain is zero; the booth keeps spawning on its normal schedule and the act clock keeps running. Misses and escapes cost the same as ever. Because a target at half speed stays on screen twice as long, the booth fills up while the bleed stops — the rescue powerup.
- Ghost Train needs a Slug chain of 5 or more targets from one shot.
- Average streak length in the log: the streak's value each time a wild shot halves or breaks it.

Expected night for the median logged player (44% accuracy, about 1.75 shots a second, cheer per second):
- Act one: payback +2.3, misses −1.0, escapes −0.3, drain −1.0, net about +0.1 — they enter act two near full.
- Act two: payback +2.3, misses −2.2 (the 1-2-4 ladder), escapes −0.5, drain −1.0, net about −1.4 — they enter act three near 30–35 cheer.
- Act three: payback +2.3, misses about −2.9 (the ladder reaches 8), escapes about −2.1 (1.3 spawns a second against 0.77 hits), drain −3.5 and rising, net about −6 — the show ends within about 6 seconds (QA's figure; the earlier −0.9 escape line undercounted).
- Night length: about 105–110 s. A 33% player dies around 65–70 s in act two; a 85% player dies around 165 s, inside the 3-minute cap; spam-clicking (3 shots a second at 18%) still dies in act one near 40 s.

Now act one is a short tutorial, act two carries the first real bleed, and act three's pressure is a drain that starts low and ramps. The 8-cheer rung of the ladder is gone: for a 44% player it needs four misses in a row and it supplied most of the cliff. Escapes cost 2 all night, still twice a wild shot. All values editable.

- Spawns per second: 0.9 / 1.0 / 1.1, with a floor of 2 / 3 / 3 live targets. Act three only reaches 1.1, so the last act is not an unfair flood; its pressure is target speed and the crowd's patience.

before.title: Rules: prizes and the night
before.text:
Prize targets
- Now and then a prize target enters the booth: a ghost, a pumpkin or a bat wearing a halo. It is the only target worth more than a normal one.
- Shooting a prize target pays a large chunk of the score and starts that type's powerup at once, for a burst of a few seconds.
- Haloes arrive on a steady cadence, dealt from a shuffled bag of the three types, so no prize repeats until the other two have had their turn. A halo only appears while no powerup is running; if one is running it waits.
- A prize target that escapes is lost: no powerup starts, it costs the same cheer as any other escape, and its type goes to the back of the bag, so the next halo is a different type.
- Ghost's halo, the Spectral Slug: for the whole burst, every shot that lands becomes a chain — it fells its target and leaps to the nearest other target, and on to the next while each is within the ghost's reach; a scattered booth stops the leap.
- Pumpkin's halo, the Candy Buckshot: for the whole burst, every shot is a fan that starts at the gun at the bottom centre of the booth, opens through the crosshair in a wide wedge, and fells every target inside that wedge.
- Bat's halo, Moonstruck: for the whole burst targets move at half speed and the crowd holds its breath, so the drain is zero; the booth keeps spawning on its normal schedule and the act clock never pauses. Misses and escapes still cost, and hits still pay. A half-speed target stays on screen twice as long, so the booth fills with easy targets while the bleed stops: this is the powerup that saves a show on its last legs, which is why it rides the hardest target to hit.
- Each target a powerup fells counts as its own hit: it extends the streak and pays its own cheer. Extra targets felled by a chain or a fan pay a flat score each rather than the multiplier, so the multiplier stays the reward for aimed shots and a burst cannot outscore the shooting around it.
- A shot fired during a burst that fells nothing is a wild shot like any other, at the same cheer cost and the same halving of the streak.

The night's acts
- The night plays in three acts on the show's own clock, which never pauses, not even for a powerup. Each act opens with a marquee cue and steps up: the booth spawns more and faster targets and the crowd's drain climbs.
- The booth spawns on its own schedule and never waits for the player to clear it, and it keeps a floor of live targets. An escape therefore always means the player let one through, never that the booth starved them at the wrong rate.
- The ending does not rely on the booth running dry. In the last act the drain keeps rising the longer the show runs, with no ceiling, so sooner or later it outruns the best payback and the curtain falls.

The results
- The curtain shows the takings, the longest streak, the prizes taken and the stamps earned. The best score is saved.
- Stamps, each one named on the results: Hot Streak — a streak that reaches the top of the multiplier. Prize Parade — all three prizes in one night. Ghost Train — a Slug chain from one shot that fells a run of targets. Last Act — reaching the third act. These four names are the only stamps; every screen uses them.

before.title: Rules: the booth and the crowd
before.text:
The loop: aim at the moving spooks, fire, and keep the streak clean. The crowd's cheer is the clock, the ammo and the ending.

Aim and fire
- Mouse: the crosshair is under the cursor; a click fires there.
- Touch: a quick tap fires at the tap point; dragging shows an offset crosshair above the finger and lifting the finger fires there, so the target is never hidden. Dragging off the booth cancels the shot.
- One shot per click or release. No ammo and no reload: a shot's only cost is the crowd's patience.
- A shot is a hit anywhere on a target's painted shape, plus a single forgiveness margin that is the same in every act. One shot destroys that target. Later acts are harder only because the targets move and arrive faster.

Hits and escapes
- A target that leaves the booth without being hit is an escape. It costs cheer but never touches the streak: you can't shoot everything, so only your own wild shots cost you.
- A hit pays back more cheer than a single wild shot costs, so accurate shooting is always the way to keep the crowd. A single wild shot is also cheaper than an escape, so a shot with a real chance of landing beats letting the target go. Only a run of misses in a row can cost more than a hit repays: the crowd spots a flail.
- Every target type pays the same. The ghost, the pumpkin and the bat differ only in how they move and how hard they are to hit.
- The first two escapes of a night are free. The first cue says this one is free and that later escapes cost cheer.

The crowd's cheer
- The cheer is the one meter besides the score. It starts full and can never rise above full; it drains all the time, and the drain climbs with the night's acts, so every show ends eventually, however clean.
- Misses in a row get dearer only as the night goes on: flat in act one, a small step up in act two, and the full ladder only in act three. Any hit resets the cost to its first step.
- It drops on a shot that hits nothing and on an escape, and every hit pays it back.
- The payback rises only over the first few hits of a streak, then holds flat while the multiplier keeps climbing. So a long streak eases the drain without ever cancelling it.
- When the cheer empties the curtain falls and the round ends. There is no countdown, no lives and no round counter.

The streak
- Every hit extends the streak, and the multiplier for a hit is the streak counting that hit, so the first hit of a night scores once and the multiplier climbs with every clean hit.
- The streak stops climbing at the top of the multiplier, so the longest streak and the best multiplier are the same height and a miss anywhere on the ladder really costs.
- A shot that hits nothing halves the streak, rounded down, and a wild shot at a streak of one clears it. Escapes leave the streak standing.
- No single miss wipes the multiplier, so a hard shot is always a bet the player can afford to make; the streak is worth steadying your aim for, not worth freezing over.

author: claude
summary: edited section “Open Questions”

before.title: Open Questions
before.text:
- Re-tune check: does the median player (under half their shots landing) reach act two with cheer to spare and last 90–120 seconds? Does a strong one reach act three but stop before about 3 minutes?
- Touch test with a first-time touch player: offset crosshair, tap to fire, drag to cancel, reaching a streak of 5. This is the biggest untested risk. Still undefined: what separates a tap from a drag; how the raised crosshair reaches the top edge of the booth; and, since the crosshair sits above the finger, aiming at the bottom edge puts the finger off the booth, which the rules say cancels the shot.
- After the re-tune, do weaker players still skip bats (under half shot)? If so, Moonstruck, the rescue powerup, rarely reaches the players who need rescuing.
- Does the act-3 ramp end strong players' shows at a satisfying moment, not abruptly? On paper the median player's act three lasts only about 6 seconds.
- Does one Slug chain or Buckshot blast restore most of the cheer meter?
- Is Moonstruck worth chasing before act three? In acts one and two the drain it stops is 1 a second, so a burst saves about 6 cheer, or nothing when cheer is already near full. Late in act three it saves about 40.
- Hits can't outpace spawns (0.9 a second in act one), so firing faster mostly adds misses. Confirm in the log that fast sweepers don't outlast aimers in act one.
- Can a new player say why they lost after the first night?
- Does the game need a pause / quit option during a night? The flowchart has none. At minimum, a browser tab losing focus must not let the never-pausing clock and drain kill the player.

author: claude
summary: edited section “Rules: prizes and the night”

before.title: Rules: prizes and the night
before.text:
Prize targets
- Now and then a prize target enters the booth: a ghost, a pumpkin or a bat wearing a halo. It is the only target worth more than a normal one.
- Shooting a prize target pays a large chunk of the score and starts that type's powerup at once, for a burst of a few seconds.
- Haloes arrive on a steady cadence, dealt from a shuffled bag of the three types, so no prize repeats until the other two have had their turn. A halo only appears while no powerup is running; if one is running it waits.
- A prize target that escapes is lost: no powerup starts, it costs the same cheer as any other escape, and its type goes to the back of the bag, so the next halo is a different type.
- Ghost's halo, the Spectral Slug: for the whole burst, every shot that lands becomes a chain — it fells its target and leaps to the nearest other target, and on to the next while each is within the ghost's reach; a scattered booth stops the leap.
- Pumpkin's halo, the Candy Buckshot: for the whole burst, every shot is a fan that starts at the gun at the bottom centre of the booth, opens through the crosshair in a wide wedge, and fells every target inside that wedge.
- Bat's halo, Moonstruck: for the whole burst targets move at half speed and the crowd holds its breath, so the drain is zero; the booth keeps spawning on its normal schedule and the act clock never pauses. Misses and escapes still cost, and hits still pay. A half-speed target stays on screen twice as long, so the booth fills with easy targets while the bleed stops: this is the powerup that saves a show on its last legs, which is why it rides the hardest target to hit.
- A powerup never builds the streak for you. The one target the shot lands on is an ordinary hit: it pays, it extends the streak, it scores the multiplier. Every extra target the chain or the fan fells pays a little cheer and a flat score, and leaves the streak exactly where it was — it neither extends nor breaks it. So a burst is a surge of points and a way to survive a crowded booth, never a shortcut to the best multiplier.
- A shot fired during a burst that fells nothing is a wild shot like any other, at the same cheer cost and the same halving of the streak.

The night's acts
- The night plays in three acts on the show's own clock, which never pauses, not even for a powerup. Each act opens with a marquee cue and steps up: the booth spawns more and faster targets and the crowd's drain climbs.
- The booth spawns on its own schedule and never waits for the player to clear it, and it keeps a floor of live targets. An escape therefore always means the player let one through, never that the booth starved them at the wrong rate.
- Only the crowd's patience ends the show. In the last act the drain starts modest and climbs every second with no ceiling, while targets are at their fastest, so the last act is the squeeze: the booth stops flooding and the meter starts running.

The results
- The curtain shows the takings, the longest streak, the prizes taken and the stamps earned. The best score is saved.
- Stamps, each one named on the results: Hot Streak — an aimed-shot streak that reaches the top of the multiplier; burst kills never add to it. Prize Parade — all three prizes in one night. Ghost Train — a Slug chain from one shot that fells a run of targets. Last Act — reaching the third act. These four names are the only stamps; every screen uses them.

before.title: Tuning starting values (from Systems, fifth pass)
before.text:
Fifth pass, two fixes. (1) Bursts no longer feed the streak: only the target the shot lands on is a hit, so Hot Streak is earned by aimed shots alone. (2) The act shape is rebuilt. The old version was a 50 s free ride followed by a cliff, because the drain, the escape cost and the miss ladder all jumped at the same moment. Now act one is a short tutorial, act two carries the first real bleed, and act three's pressure is a drain that starts low and ramps. The 8-cheer rung of the ladder is gone: for a 44% player it needs four misses in a row and it supplied most of the cliff. Escapes cost 2 all night, still twice a wild shot. All values editable.

- Cheer: 100, never above 100. Drain per second: act 1 = 0.5, act 2 = 1.0, act 3 = 2.0 rising 0.18 every second with no ceiling. Acts begin at 0 / 40 / 80 s.
- Payback per hit: 2.5 for the first hit of a streak, plus 0.25 for each further step, capped at 3.5 (reached at streak 5).
- Wild shot cost: flat 1 for all of act one. From act two on: 1, then 2, then 4, capped at 4. Any hit resets it to the first step. The streak halves. A burst shot that fells nothing counts as a wild shot.
- Escape: 2 cheer all night, the streak untouched; the first two escapes of a night are free.
- Burst kills: the target the shot lands on is an ordinary hit — it pays the multiplier, pays cheer and extends the streak. Every extra target a chain or fan fells pays 1 cheer and the flat 150 score, and neither extends nor breaks the streak. So a 6 s burst adds at most as many streak steps as the player took aimed shots.
- Streak and multiplier: the streak stops at 10, which is also the top multiplier; a hit's multiplier is the streak counting that hit.
- Score: a normal target pays 100 x multiplier; a prize target pays 500 x multiplier plus its powerup; every extra target felled by a chain or fan pays a flat 150.
- Hit shape: the painted shape plus a margin of 25% of the target's widest dimension, the same in every act.
- Target speed in booth widths per second: ghost 0.12 drifting, pumpkin 0.18 bouncing, bat 0.30 swooping. Act speed multiplier 1.0 / 1.2 / 1.45.
- Spawns per second: 0.9 / 1.0 / 1.1, with a floor of 2 / 3 / 3 live targets. Act three only reaches 1.1, so the last act is not an unfair flood; its pressure is target speed and the crowd's patience.
- Halo about every 25 s from a shuffled bag of the three types; a halo waits while a burst runs. Every burst lasts 6 s.
- Spectral Slug reach: 20% of the booth's width, measured from the last felled target and re-checked against the nearest remaining target on each leap.
- Candy Buckshot: fan from the muzzle at the bottom centre, centred on the crosshair, half-angle 20 degrees, reaching the top of the booth; it fells every target whose centre is inside. Applies to every shot during the burst.
- Moonstruck: for the 6 s burst, targets move at half speed and the passive drain is zero; the booth keeps spawning on its normal schedule and the act clock keeps running. Misses and escapes cost the same as ever.
- Ghost Train needs a Slug chain of 5 or more targets from one shot.
- Average streak length in the log: the streak's value each time a wild shot halves or breaks it.

Expected night for the median logged player (44% accuracy, about 1.75 shots a second; cheer per second, all four lines):
- Act one (0–40 s): payback +2.3, misses −1.0, escapes −0.3, drain −0.5, net about +0.5, so the cheer sits at full. Act one is the tutorial, not a threat.
- Act two (40–80 s): payback +2.3, misses −2.3, escapes −0.5, drain −1.0, net about −1.5; they enter act three near 40 cheer.
- Act three (80 s on): payback +2.3, misses −2.3, escapes −0.7, drain −2.0 rising 0.18, net about −2.7 at the start and −3.5 ten seconds later; act three lasts 13–15 s.
- Night length: about 90–95 s. A 33% player dies around 70 s, in act two. An 85% player lasts about 115–120 s, and about 130 s with one Moonstruck in act three — inside the 3-minute cap. Spam-clicking (3 shots a second at 18%) dies at about 45 s as act one closes.

before.title: Rules: prizes and the night
before.text:
Prize targets
- Now and then a prize target enters the booth: a ghost, a pumpkin or a bat wearing a halo. It is the only target worth more than a normal one.
- Shooting a prize target pays a large chunk of the score and starts that type's powerup at once, for a burst of a few seconds.
- Haloes arrive on a steady cadence, dealt from a shuffled bag of the three types, so no prize repeats until the other two have had their turn. A halo only appears while no powerup is running; if one is running it waits.
- A prize target that escapes is lost: no powerup starts, it costs the same cheer as any other escape, and its type goes to the back of the bag, so the next halo is a different type.
- Ghost's halo, the Spectral Slug: for the whole burst, every shot that lands becomes a chain — it fells its target and leaps to the nearest other target, and on to the next while each is within the ghost's reach; a scattered booth stops the leap.
- Pumpkin's halo, the Candy Buckshot: for the whole burst, every shot is a fan that starts at the gun at the bottom centre of the booth, opens through the crosshair in a wide wedge, and fells every target inside that wedge.
- Bat's halo, Moonstruck: for the whole burst targets move at half speed and the crowd holds its breath, so the drain is zero; the booth keeps spawning on its normal schedule and the act clock never pauses. Misses and escapes still cost, and hits still pay. A half-speed target stays on screen twice as long, so the booth fills with easy targets while the bleed stops: this is the powerup that saves a show on its last legs, which is why it rides the hardest target to hit.
- A powerup never builds the streak for you. The one target the shot lands on is an ordinary hit: it pays, it extends the streak, it scores the multiplier. Every extra target the chain or the fan fells pays a little cheer and a flat score, and leaves the streak exactly where it was — it neither extends nor breaks it. So a burst is a surge of points and a way to survive a crowded booth, never a shortcut to the best multiplier.
- A shot fired during a burst that fells nothing is a wild shot like any other, at the same cheer cost and the same halving of the streak.

The night's acts
- The night plays in three acts on the show's own clock, which never pauses for anything in the show, not even a powerup. Only the player's Pause (or the tab losing focus) freezes it, along with everything else. Each act opens with a marquee cue and steps up: the booth spawns more and faster targets and the crowd's drain climbs.

before.title: Rules: the booth and the crowd
before.text:
The loop: aim at the moving spooks, fire, and keep the streak clean. The crowd's cheer is the clock, the ammo and the ending.

Aim and fire
- Mouse: the crosshair is under the cursor; a click fires there.
- Touch: a quick tap fires at the tap point; dragging shows an offset crosshair above the finger and lifting the finger fires there, so the target is never hidden. Dragging off the booth cancels the shot.
- One shot per click or release. No ammo and no reload: a shot's only cost is the crowd's patience.
- A shot is a hit anywhere on a target's painted shape, plus a single forgiveness margin that is the same in every act. One shot destroys that target. Later acts are harder only because the targets move and arrive faster.

Hits and escapes
- A target that leaves the booth without being hit is an escape. It costs cheer but never touches the streak: you can't shoot everything, so only your own wild shots cost you.
- A hit pays back more cheer than a single wild shot costs, so accurate shooting is always the way to keep the crowd. A single wild shot is also cheaper than an escape, so a shot with a real chance of landing beats letting the target go. Only a run of misses in a row can cost more than a hit repays: the crowd spots a flail.
- Every target type pays the same. The ghost, the pumpkin and the bat differ only in how they move and how hard they are to hit.
- The first two escapes of a night are free. The first cue says this one is free and that later escapes cost cheer.

The crowd's cheer
- The cheer is the one meter besides the score. It starts full and can never rise above full; it drains all the time, and the drain climbs with the night's acts, so every show ends eventually, however clean.
- Misses in a row get dearer exactly once, when act two begins, and the cost has a fixed ceiling from then on; from act two the ladder does not get any steeper. The crowd's growing impatience shows in the drain, not in the price of a miss. Any hit resets the cost to its first step.
- It drops on a shot that hits nothing and on an escape, and every hit pays it back.
- The payback rises only over the first few hits of a streak, then holds flat while the multiplier keeps climbing. So a long streak eases the drain without ever cancelling it.
- When the cheer empties the curtain falls and the round ends. There is no countdown, no lives and no round counter.

The streak
- Every hit extends the streak, and the multiplier for a hit is the streak counting that hit, so the first hit of a night scores once and the multiplier climbs with every clean hit.
- The streak stops climbing at the top of the multiplier, so the longest streak and the best multiplier are the same height and a miss anywhere on the ladder really costs.
- A shot that hits nothing halves the streak, rounded down, and a wild shot at a streak of one clears it. Escapes leave the streak standing.
- No single miss wipes the multiplier, so a hard shot is always a bet the player can afford to make; the streak is worth steadying your aim for, not worth freezing over.

before.title: Open Questions
before.text:
- Re-tune check: does the median player (under half their shots landing) reach act two with cheer to spare and last 90–120 seconds? Does a strong one reach act three but stop before about 3 minutes?
- Touch test with a first-time touch player: offset crosshair, tap to fire, drag to cancel, reaching a streak of 5. This is the biggest untested risk. Still undefined: what separates a tap from a drag; how the raised crosshair reaches the top edge of the booth; and, since the crosshair sits above the finger, aiming at the bottom edge puts the finger off the booth, which the rules say cancels the shot.
- Candy Buckshot gap (QA): a fan shot whose crosshair is on empty space but whose wedge fells targets has no stated rule. Is it a hit, a wild shot, or neutral?
- After the re-tune, do weaker players still skip bats (under half shot)? If so, Moonstruck, the rescue powerup, rarely reaches the players who need rescuing.

before.title: Playtest 1 results (7 mouse runs)
before.text:
- Every night is far too short: 15 to 60 seconds against a 90 to 120 second target. Nobody reached act three; two runs reached act two.
- Accuracy across the seven runs: 18%, 29%, 39%, 44%, 49%, 53%, 68%. The median player hits under half their shots, at about 1.5 to 2 shots a second. Tune for that player, not for the best run.
- Wild shots are the biggest cheer loss in every run, bigger than the drain and the escapes. The wild-shot ladder is too harsh, as QA predicted.
- Hits pay back far too little: a hit refills less than one wild shot costs, so missing a little outweighs hitting a lot.
- Escapes are too frequent for most players (about 15 to 35 a minute), so the booth spawns faster than people can shoot.
- The streak mostly stays low: it averages 1 to 4 at each break, under the target of 5. Good runs still hit long streaks (12 and 31).
- Spraying dies fast (2.6 shots a second at 18% accuracy died in 15 seconds), so the anti-spray rule works and can be softened.
- Weaker players skip bats (10 to 27% shot); stronger ones shoot about half.
- Ghost Train is reachable: one Slug chain hit 7.
- Touch is untested: every shot was a mouse click.
- The build's tuning differs from the Brief in places (act-one hit margin, prize score, Buckshot width, Moonstruck speed); match it to the Brief before the next test.

after.title: Playtest results
after.text:
Playtest 1 (7 mouse runs, old tuning): nights of 15–60 s, nobody reached act three. Accuracy 18–68%, median 44%. Wild shots were the biggest cheer loss, hits paid back less than a miss cost, and weaker players skipped bats.

Playtest 2 (1 mouse run, sixth-pass tuning):
- 58% accuracy at about 1.5 shots a second: the night lasted 112 s and reached act three, with 32 s in the last act. Cheer entering acts two and three was 95 and 64, matching the paper estimate.
- The re-tune works: the night is inside the 90–120 s target, and the median-player maths holds up.
- Wild shots still cost more cheer than escapes, but the drain is now the biggest loss, as intended.
- Escapes are still high at about 17 a minute.
- Half the bats were shot. The host reports bats are small and fast but hittable.
- Three of the four stamps (Hot Streak, Prize Parade, Last Act) were earned in one ordinary night, so stamps will run out too fast.
- No Slug chain reached Ghost Train's length (best was 3).
- Touch is still untested: every shot was a mouse click.
- The build's touch values differ from the Art Director's rules (the cancel strip is on the right only, and the crosshair offset and drag threshold differ).

before.title: Rules: prizes and the night
before.text:
Prize targets
- Now and then a prize target enters the booth: a ghost, a pumpkin or a bat wearing a halo. It is the only target worth more than a normal one.
- A halo steadies its wearer: a prize target always drifts at the ghost's slow pace, whatever its type, so the prize is visible and catchable even for a player who is not landing much. That is why the rescue powerup is not hidden behind the hardest target in the booth.
- Shooting a prize target pays a large chunk of the score and starts that type's powerup at once, for a burst of a few seconds.
- Haloes arrive on a steady cadence, dealt from a shuffled bag of the three types, so no prize repeats until the other two have had their turn. A halo only appears while no powerup is running; if one is running it waits.
- A prize target that escapes is lost: no powerup starts, it costs the same cheer as any other escape, and its type goes to the back of the bag, so the next halo is a different type.
- Ghost's halo, the Spectral Slug: for the whole burst, every shot that lands becomes a chain — it fells its target and leaps to the nearest other target, and on to the next while each is within the ghost's reach; a scattered booth stops the leap.
- Pumpkin's halo, the Candy Buckshot: for the whole burst, every shot is a fan that starts at the gun at the bottom centre of the booth, opens through the crosshair in a wide wedge, and fells every target inside that wedge.
- Bat's halo, Moonstruck: for the whole burst targets move at half speed and the crowd holds its breath, so the drain is zero; the booth keeps spawning on its normal schedule and the act clock never pauses. Misses and escapes still cost, and hits still pay. A half-speed target stays on screen twice as long, so the booth fills with easy targets while the bleed stops.
- The crosshair decides every shot, burst or not. A target under the crosshair is a hit: it pays, it scores the multiplier and it extends the streak. Empty booth under the crosshair is a wild shot: it costs the cheer a wild shot costs and halves the streak, even when a fan or a chain fells targets anyway. Extras still pay.
- Every extra target a chain or a fan fells pays a little cheer and a flat score, and leaves the streak exactly where it was — it neither extends nor breaks it. So a powerup is a surge of points and a way to survive a crowded booth, never a shortcut to the best multiplier: Hot Streak is earned only by aimed shots.
- Aiming a fan between targets therefore buys safety at the price of the streak, which is a real trade during a burst and a bad habit outside one.

The night's acts
- The night plays in three acts on the show's own clock, which never pauses except on the Pause screen. Each act opens with a marquee cue and steps up: the booth spawns more and faster targets and the crowd's drain climbs.
- The booth spawns on its own schedule and never waits for the player to clear it, and it keeps a floor of live targets. An escape therefore always means the player let one through, never that the booth starved them at the wrong rate.
- Only the crowd's patience ends the show (the Pause screen excepted). In the last act the drain starts modest and climbs every second with no ceiling, while targets are at their fastest, so the last act is the squeeze: the booth stops flooding and the meter starts running.

The results
- The curtain shows the takings, the longest streak, the prizes taken and the stamps earned. The best score is saved.
- Stamps, each one named on the results: Hot Streak — an aimed-shot streak that reaches the top of the multiplier; burst kills never add to it. Prize Parade — all three prizes in one night. Ghost Train — a Slug chain from one shot that fells a run of targets. Last Act — reaching the third act. These four names are the only stamps; every screen uses them.
